"Mouldwarp" (also spelled "moldwarp" or "mouldiwarp") is indeed a historical English term for a mole. The word comes from Middle English and has Germanic roots, literally meaning "earth-thrower" (from "mould" meaning earth/soil and "warp" meaning to throw). This term was commonly used in medieval and early modern English to refer to the burrowing mammal we now simply call a mole.
